subject.title: [Feature]: Skill lifecycle management — auto-optimization on failure + usage-based retirement

question: Should failure-driven skill repair and usage-based skill retirement be first-class OpenClaw core behavior, a new plugin API/ClawHub package, or separate narrower tracks?
rationale: The current source has a proposal-first correction path but not failure/performance scoring or retirement, and choosing where to persist metrics or hide/delete skills is a product, privacy, and extension-boundary decision.

options.title: Design the core/API boundary first
options.body: Define the minimal core telemetry and proposal hooks, plus default-off archive/delete policy, before asking for implementation.

options.title: Keep it as a plugin/ClawHub experiment
options.body: Treat lifecycle analytics and retirement UI as an external package unless the experiment proves a missing core API.

options.title: Split the issue into narrower decisions
options.body: Track failure-repair proposals separately from usage retirement so each can move with its own privacy, storage, and UX design.

recommendation.title: Design the core/API boundary first
recommendation.body: Define the minimal core telemetry and proposal hooks, plus default-off archive/delete policy, before asking for implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has the strongest current-main history across the active auto-capture and Skill Workshop config/type code that the decision would extend.
